correctness.rationale: For h=mn/2, the graph-state coefficient array has entries p^{-h} ω^{uᵀDv}. Grouping u by the image of Dᵀ gives p^r orthogonal Fourier characters on B and orthogonal sums on A, each sum of p^{h−r} computational basis states. This gives the stated flat Schmidt spectrum and entropy. The full adjacency has rank 2r. The frozen local-algebra proof checks out: τ=x+x^{-1}+y+y^{-1} factors as (x+y)(1+xy)/(xy). After separating p-parts P,Q and prime-to-p parts M,N, there are 2gcd(M,N)−4 one-branch points of length min(P,Q), plus two crossings. At a crossing the module with s^P=0 is free on 1,t by the monic relation t²=s²(1+t)/(1+s). It has t^{2P}=0; for Q>P, Q≥3P makes t^Q redundant. For P=Q the additionally imposed t^P generates a one-dimensional socle ideal, as it is a unit times s^{P−1}t. The same reasoning includes P=Q=1 and symmetry covers Q<P. An independent proof of the all-size nullity avoids the local computation: up to a unit shift the adjacency is (I+S)(I+H), where S,H are the (1,−1) and (1,1) shifts. Conjugation by multiplication by (−1)^i gives A=I−S and B=I−H. Each shift has g orbits, labeled by i+j and i−j modulo g respectively. Nullity of AB equals g+dim(ker A ∩ im B). On ker A, testing im B amounts to pairing with the orbit indicators in ker Bᵀ. Two labeled orbits have intersection 0 for different parity and 2mn/g² for the same parity: the map (i,j)↦(i+j,i−j) mod g has a two-element kernel on residues and image the equal-parity pairs. Hence the test matrix has two constant blocks, of total rank 2 when p∤2mn/g² and rank 0 otherwise. For odd p this is precisely the equal-valuation dichotomy. Nullity of the full adjacency is 2g−2δ, yielding all stated example ranks and entropies without any large-size extrapolation.
residual_risks: The recorded 420 modular grid comparisons (310 equal and 110 unequal valuations) and 15 local length checks are finite; they were not rerun and are not used to prove the all-size result. The proof applies to the specified simple toroidal grid with even side lengths at least four; changes to edge multiplicities or boundary conditions are not covered.

evidence: Hein et al. give the binary cut-rank reduction, and the qudit sources give the controlled-phase/finite-field adjacency setting. Zaidenberg formulates periodic convolution kernel dimension and identifies harmonic characters via torsion points for periods coprime to p.

The 2004 σ-automata paper is plausibly relevant, but the abstract accessible in the search results does not settle its boundary model or rank formula. Its full text was not obtained from the DOI/publisher, the identified university site, or an accessible public alternate.

evidence: The binary result and graph-state machinery do not produce the odd-p correction. When evaluating the same factorization at arbitrary periods, one must compute either the crossing quotient lengths or the pairing of kernels of the two shift factors. In the latter calculation the two parity blocks have common scalar 2mn/g², which may vanish at an odd prime exactly when the valuations differ.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Standard cut rank supplies the interpretation, and semisimple torsion-point counting handles periods prime to p, but the exact arithmetic of the interaction is not supplied by these source statements. Counting zero characters alone would omit the nonsemisimple contribution. Thus only the valuation-sensitive all-period rank calculation and its spectral consequences are credited.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct content is the closed odd-prime toroidal adjacency nullity, equivalently exact checkerboard entanglement, and its one-dit valuation switch. The same-graph binary formula, the standard graph-state cut-rank reduction and characteristic-p convolution machinery are not new. No verified checked source covers the odd-prime switch for this graph and these side-length hypotheses, including inseparable periods. This is a bounded comparative judgment, not a priority certificate.
residual_risks: No historical priority is inferred from same-day path dates or a search miss. value.rationale: Checkerboard entropy is a natural invariant of the periodic grid state. The formula isolates the exact departure from the generic deficit at fixed geometry, distinguishes equal nonzero valuations from unequal ones, and explains why a semisimple character count is insufficient. It settles a complete arithmetic classification for this cut rather than a tabulation of examples or a repackaging of the usual cut-rank identity.
residual_risks: The result measures pure-state entanglement and says nothing about robustness, preparation complexity, weighted graphs, or composite dimensions.
